subject.title: Feature: fire session-memory hook on session reset/prune, not just compaction

question: Which reset/prune memory-preservation contract should OpenClaw support before outgoing session state is rolled over or deleted?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the permanent fix affects plugin-visible hook semantics, transcript exposure, async deletion timing, memory persistence, and potentially security-sensitive content retention, so automation should not choose the contract alone.

options.title: Define a typed lifecycle surface
options.body: Add or extend a session lifecycle hook that explicitly covers before-reset and before-prune with documented payload, timing, timeout, and privacy semantics, then wire session-memory to that contract.

options.title: Refine the active daily/idle PR first
options.body: Accept the daily/idle reset part through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/61675 after rebase/proof and keep prune as a separate follow-up item.

options.title: Use existing plugin/external memory paths
options.body: Decline new core reset/prune hook behavior and require memory plugins or external snapshot systems to use existing session_end/session_start or continuous-persistence patterns.

recommendation.title: Define a typed lifecycle surface
recommendation.body: Add or extend a session lifecycle hook that explicitly covers before-reset and before-prune with documented payload, timing, timeout, and privacy semantics, then wire session-memory to that contract.
